# Report: `region_006` (region.fasta)

## Verdict
The region is **not** anonymous "junk" DNA — it is a **gene-dense protein-coding region, almost certainly bacterial**, dominated by genes on the **minus (reverse-complement) strand**. Two complete genes lie on that strand, the 3′ end of a third gene lies on the plus strand at the left edge, and the extraction window appears to cut coding sequence at *both* ends. All coordinates below are 1-based, inclusive, on the given strand.

## Basic statistics
- Length 3,000 bp; A 651 / T 702 / G 764 / C 883; **GC 54.9%**; no ambiguous or non-ACGT characters.

## Predicted genes

| Feature | Strand | Coordinates | Size | Start / stop codons |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ORF-A | minus | **1484–2935** | 1452 bp, 483 aa | ATG 2933–2935 / TAG 1484–1486 |
| ORF-B | minus | **295–1176** | 882 bp, 293 aa | ATG 1174–1176 / TGA 295–297 |
| ORF-C (partial) | plus | **1–297** (visible) | ≥98 aa, 5′-truncated | stop TAA 298–300 |

**ORF-A (1484–2935, minus).** Protein is Leu-rich (66 Leu = 13.7%), 44% hydrophobic, net charge ≈ −3, with two borderline hydrophobic segments (aa 94–112, 128–146; KD ≈ 1.7 — below a convincing TM-helix threshold). Its reading frame contains **no stop codon from 2935 up to the window edge (3000)**, so the true 5′ end probably lies outside the window; in-window alternatives are GTG 2990–2992 (501 aa) and GTG 2942–2944.

**ORF-B (295–1176, minus).** Small acidic protein, net charge −13, 32% charged residues, no TM segment. Appears complete within the window.

**ORF-C (1–297, plus).** Weakest call, but coding-like: the plus frame-0 reading is stop-free across the entire 1–297 segment (98 codons) and ends at a TAA at 298–300. Its own codon-position GC bias (GC1/GC2/GC3 = 59.2 / **36.7** / 67.3, the classic GC2 depression) and avoidance of AT-rich codons (TTA 0, CTA 0, TCA 1) match the other two genes — this segment lies *outside* ORF-B, so its signal is independent. Only in-frame *internal* starts exist (GTG 136, TTG 142, ATG 154), so the real start is upstream, outside the window.

Minus-strand layout (5′→3′ = coordinate 3000→1): ORF-A (2935→1484) → **intergenic gap 1177–1483 (307 bp, GC 49.8%)** → ORF-B (1176→295). ORF-A and ORF-B are adjacent, same-strand, and could form one transcriptional unit; ORF-C's 3′ end (stop at 298–300) abuts ORF-B's stop (295–297) on the opposite strand — a compact, partially convergent arrangement typical of dense bacterial genomes.

## Evidence these are real genes (not chance ORFs)
- **Stop-free run significance:** the minus strand has stop-free runs of 504 codons (ORF-A's frame) and 358 codons (ORF-B's frame). Under 500 trinucleotide-composition-preserving shuffles, a ≥484-codon run occurred **0/500** times (best-frame max was 400; mean 202) and ≥358 occurred 3/500 (p ≈ 0.006).
- **Codon-position GC bias** (coding signature): ORF-A 67.4/40.7/61.6, ORF-B 61.2/39.1/60.2 (GC2 dips to ~40% vs 55% background).
- **High-GC-genome codon usage:** Leu is 59% (ORF-A) and 64% (ORF-B) CTG; Arg uses **zero** AGA/AGG codons in both genes (all CGN); ORF-B contains a single TTA/CTA-type codon in 294 codons. This pattern (avoidance of AT-rich synonymous codons) fits a moderately GC-rich bacterium with actinobacteria-like usage.

## A caution about the plus strand
Naive ORF-finding also lights up the plus strand (stop-free stretches of 343 codons at 301–1332, 152 at 2136–2594, 122 at 1436–1804). These are largely **artifacts**: the frames at 301–1332 and 1436–1804 are the codon-*aligned complements* of the real minus-strand genes. Because the genes avoid TTA/CTA/TCA — whose reverse complements are precisely the stops TAA/TAG/TGA — the complementary frame is automatically stop-free. I verified this directly: ORF-B contains exactly one TTA codon (at 298–300), and that is exactly where the complementary plus-frame run breaks (TAA at 298–300). The 343-codon run is within the range expected from composition alone (95th percentile of the shuffled null = 278 codons). Only ORF-C (1–297) carries an *independent* coding signature on the plus strand.

## Regulatory and other features (mostly absent)
- **No Shine-Dalgarno core** (AGGAGG-class) within 25 nt 5′ of either minus-strand start — consistent with high-GC bacteria, or with the in-window ATGs being internal (ORF-A) — flanks: ORF-B `GCCGTTGTCGACACCCTCGACCAA`; ORF-A `CGCCGACGGCGCGACCAGCACGGCTCTAAGCGTGCTGGCG`.
- **No σ70-consensus promoter** (TTGACA…TATAAT) in the intergenic gap; best −35-like hexamer is TTGACT at 1417–1422 (one mismatch), ~245 nt from ORF-B's start — too far to be its promoter.
- **No convincing rho-independent terminator**: no hairpin (stem ≥ 6 bp) followed closely by a U-run 3′ of either minus-strand gene; the only nearby candidates (6-bp-stem hairpin at 1441–1456; mRNA U-run at 1421–1424) are separated by ~16 nt, which is atypical.
- **No tRNA-like or CRISPR-like repeat structures.**
- **Homopolymers:** a single notable run, T₆ at 1463–1468 (in the intergenic gap).
- **Direct repeat:** a 12-bp exact repeat, `GAATGCGATTAT`, at **1360–1371** (intergenic gap) and **2479–2490** (inside ORF-A); flanking 30-bp windows share only 18/30 identities, so it is probably coincidental, but worth recording.
- **Restriction sites** (scattered, roughly chance density for 55% GC DNA; no polylinker-like cluster): PstI 19, EcoRI 127, BglII 386, HindIII 508, EcoRV 697 and 1544, SphI 951, SalI 1189, NcoI 1780, NdeI 1994, AatII/BsaHI 2507, KpnI 2895.
- **Perfect palindromes:** two 10-bp inverted repeats, GCTTATAAGC at 1552–1561 and GGCTTAAGCC at 2863–2872 (both within ORF-A) — approximately chance density.

## Could not be determined
No function can be assigned from sequence alone (no database available): neither protein contains recognizable motifs (no P-loop/Walker A, twin-arginine, or Zn-binding CxxC…CxxC patterns), and no organism-level identification is possible. The most defensible statement is that region_006 is a ~55% GC, protein-coding window with high-GC-genome codon usage, two complete minus-strand ORFs (483 aa and 293 aa) separated by a 307-bp noncoding gap, plus the 3′ ~98 codons of a plus-strand gene at the left edge, with the window likely truncating genes at both ends (positions 1 and 3000).
